title: Christa Pike: What happens when executions go wrong?
description:
Last week, Christa Pike, a death row inmate in the US faced execution via lethal injection for a murder she committed in 1995. But after she was given two full doses of the drug pentobarbital, she survived. At the time of uploading this podcast, she remains awake in hospital and it’s unclear what went wrong with the attempted execution.

We hear the details from BBC reporters in the US, who have been covering this story including Brandon Drenon, Kayla Epstein and Nada Tawfik.

Not long after Pike’s recovery, the US Defence Secretary, Pete Hegseth, announced that an execution by firing squad in Fort Hood, Texas will be livestreamed to the public for the first time. The man on death row is Nidal Hasan, a former US Army major and he shot dead 13 unarmed US soldiers in 2009.

What does this all mean for the future of the death penalty in the US?

summaryEn: This episode of What in the World examines the death penalty in the United States, focusing on the botched execution of death row inmate Christa Pike. Convicted for a 1995 murder, Pike survived after receiving two doses of pentobarbital during a lethal injection attempt in Tennessee. The incident has raised serious questions about the reliability and humaneness of lethal injections, as well as the scarcity and potential degradation of execution drugs. Following the failed execution, the Governor of Tennessee paused all executions in the state for the rest of the year and ordered an independent review, while Pike's attorneys are seeking to commute her sentence to life imprisonment. The episode also discusses the controversial decision by the US Defence Secretary to publicly livestream the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, a former US Army major who killed 13 unarmed soldiers in 2009.
